{{Use Australian English|date=October 2011}}

'''Michael A. O'Keefe''' (born 8 September 1942, in [[East Melbourne]], [[Australia]]) is a physicist who has worked in [[materials science]] and [[electron microscopy]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://myprofile.cos.com/maokeefe |title=Profile |accessdate=25 March 2009 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070701163517/http://myprofile.cos.com/maokeefe |archivedate=1 July 2007  }}</ref> He is perhaps best known for his production of the seminal computer code for modeling of [[high-resolution transmission electron microscopy]] (HRTEM) images;<ref>{{Cite journal|url=http://www.nature.com/nature/journal/v274/n5669/pdf/274322a0.pdf|doi=10.1038/274322a0|title=Computed crystal structure images for high resolution electron microscopy|year=1978|last1=O'Keefe|first1=M. A.|last2=Buseck|first2=P. R.|last3=Iijima|first3=S.|journal=Nature|volume=274|issue=5669|pages=322–324|bibcode=1978Natur.274..322O|s2cid=4163994}}</ref> his software was later made available<ref>{{cite web | url=http://repositories.cdlib.org/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=2193&context=lbnl | title=OLIS: On-Line Image Simulation and structure characterization for the Materials Microcharacterization Collaboratory }}</ref> as part of the DeepView package<ref>{{Cite book|chapter-url=http://portal.acm.org/citation.cfm?id=331532.331597|doi = 10.1145/331532.331597|chapter = Deep ''View''|title = Proceedings of the 1999 ACM/IEEE conference on Supercomputing (CDROM) - Supercomputing '99|year = 1999|last1 = Parvin|first1 = B.|last2 = Taylor|first2 = J.|last3 = Cong|first3 = G.|last4 = Okeefe|first4 = M. A.|last5 = Barcellos-Hoff|first5 = M. H.|pages = 65–es|isbn = 1581130910|s2cid = 6469606}}</ref> for remote electron microscopy<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lbl.gov/Publications/Currents/Archive/June-12-1998.html#RTFToC19|title = Berkeley Lab Currents -- June 12, 1998}}</ref> and control.<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.lbl.gov/Publications/Currents/Archive/Jan-28-2000.html#RTFToC3 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210413010733/http://www.lbl.gov/Publications/Currents/Archive/Jan-28-2000.html#RTFToC3 | title=Look Deep, Look Far: Remote Microscopy and Telescopy | first=Paul | last=Preuss | archive-date=2021-04-13}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web | url=https://escholarship.org/uc/item/45m674rm | title=Automation for on-line remote-control in-situ electron microscopy | access-date=2024-06-01 | website=escholarship.org | author1=O'Keefe, M.| author2=Parvin, B.| author3=Owen, D. | author4=Taylor, J. | author5=Westmacott, K.| author6= Johnston, W.| author7=Dahmen, U. | publisher=Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory}}</ref>  O'Keefe's tutorial on theory and application of high-resolution electron microscope image simulation is available online.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.osti.gov/bridge/product.biblio.jsp?osti_id=10196824|title = Interpretation of HRTEM images by image simulation: An introduction to theory and practice|date = August 1994|last1 = O'Keefe|first1 = M. A.}}</ref>

O'Keefe has established methods of quantifying resolution quality, and methods of deriving accurate atom positions from high-resolution images.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://jmicro.oxfordjournals.org/cgi/reprint/dfi036v1?ijkey=mu0saz89qPTCjoq&keytype=ref |title=HRTEM imaging of atoms at sub-Ångström resolution |accessdate=8 July 2010 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://archive.today/20120713075354/http://jmicro.oxfordjournals.org/cgi/reprint/dfi036v1?ijkey=mu0saz89qPTCjoq&keytype=ref |archivedate=13 July 2012  }}</ref>  He used these methods to help establish high-resolution electron microscopy as a precise science; in addition to its more-pedestrian role of pictorial confirmation of nano measurements, he demonstrated HRTEM's value in measurement of nano-properties.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.osti.gov/bridge/purl.cover.jsp;jsessionid=A41080E8B4C9912AE00EC4D1BD6AC35C?purl=/821768-E3YVgN/native/ | title=Sub-Angstrom electron microscopy for sub-Angstrom nano-metrology | date=18 January 2004 | last1=O'Keefe | first1=Michael A. | last2=Allard | first2=Lawrence F. }}</ref>  The video<ref>{{cite AV media |url=http://www-conf.slac.stanford.edu/dmw2004/slacworkshop/ram/DM16pm1d.ram |title=Workshop |accessdate=26 March 2009 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20081113011826/http://www-conf.slac.stanford.edu/dmw2004/slacworkshop/ram/DM16pm1d.ram |archive-date=2008-11-13}}</ref> and associated slides<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www-conf.slac.stanford.edu/dmw2004/slacworkshop/talks/anderson/DMW_Nano.ppt | format=PPT | title=Data Management workshop - Nanosciences | date=2004-03-16 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130629160606/http://www-conf.slac.stanford.edu/dmw2004/slacworkshop/talks/anderson/DMW_Nano.ppt | archive-date=2013-06-29}}</ref> illustrate the role of his work in providing tools for nano-characterization.

O'Keefe designed and developed the one-[[Ångström]] microscope (OÅM) for the [[National Center for Electron Microscopy]] at [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]] based on an [[FEI Company]] CM300 microscope that he modified extensively to improve coherence and correct three-fold astigmatism.  He was successful in breaking the "one-Ångström barrier" to resolution using his combination of hardware and software correction of microscope aberrations.  He produced the first HRTEM images to show [[carbon]] atoms separated by less than one Ångström in [[diamond]] (0.89 Å)<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/science/nature/365866.stm|title=BBC News &#124; Sci/Tech &#124; Scientists see atoms in diamond}}</ref> and [[silicon]] atoms in crystalline silicon (0.78 Å)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lbl.gov/Publications/Currents/Archive/May-18-2001.html#_Hlk514817949|title=Berkeley Lab Currents -- May 18, 2001}}</ref>—an example of his silicon work appears on a webpage at the Department of Energy.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sc.doe.gov/bes/scale_of_things.html |title=The Scale of Things |accessdate=31 January 2010 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100201175106/http://www.sc.doe.gov/bes/scale_of_things.html |archivedate=1 February 2010 }}</ref>  His OÅM was the first HRTEM able to image the smallest metal atoms ([[lithium]]) in [[lithium battery]] materials.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=http://www.nature.com/nmat/journal/v2/n7/abs/nmat922.html|doi = 10.1038/nmat922|title = Atomic resolution of lithium ions in LiCoO2|year = 2003|last1 = Shao-Horn|first1 = Yang|last2 = Croguennec|first2 = Laurence|author2-link=Laurence Croguennec|last3 = Delmas|first3 = Claude|last4 = Nelson|first4 = E. Chris|last5 = O'Keefe|first5 = Michael A.|journal = Nature Materials|volume = 2|issue = 7|pages = 464–467|pmid = 12806387|bibcode = 2003NatMa...2..464S|s2cid = 34357573}}</ref>  Building on his work designing and operating his one-[[Ångström]] microscope (OÅM), O'Keefe produced the design for the LBNL TEAM (transmission electron aspheric microscope) able to resolve atoms in the deep sub-Ångström resolution region (less than 0.5 Å) using a hardware electron-wave phase-corrector (Cs corrector) in combination with a coherence-enhancing electron-beam monochromator.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://escholarship.org/uc/item/9hw681vh | title=HRTEM at half-Angstrom resolution: From OAM to TEAM | year=2003 | access-date=2024-06-01}}</ref>

O'Keefe was elected president of the [[Microscopy Society of America]] in 2007.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://microscopy.org/past-presidents|title=MSA Past Presidents|publisher= Microscopy Society of America|accessdate= 15 April 2025}}</ref>
